learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of both mathematical principles and the role of mathematical sciences as a tool for the analysis and the problem solving of mechanical engineering problems. Knowledge of the principles of computer science and the algorithmic and numerical approach to problems.

Applying knowledge and understanding related to mathematical methods - with particular reference to differential equations, large-scale linear and nonlinear systems - to model, analyze and solve engineering problems, also with the help of IT tools.
Development of an adequate expression and technical discussion of own arguments

syllabus_topics: Direct methods for sparse linear systems
Iterative methods for nonlinear systems of equations
Numerical methods for the Cauchy problem
Numerical methods for boundary value problems
Numerical methods for partial differential equations
assessment_rules: Students' evaluation will consist of a colloquium on numerical methodologies. Grading ranges from Fail (Insufficient) for serious conceptual errors to Excellent or outstanding (29-30 and Honors) for complete, in-depth, and well-structured knowledge, critical thinking, originality, and rigor. Honors (Laude) is awarded for work or performance distinguished by brilliance and originality. Minimum passing grade is 18.
